text:
talya: FYI customer (acme-inc) just escalated — their prod job started failing at ~07:30 UTC with NXDOMAIN when hitting api.svc.internal.redwood from within their VPC. Works from our bastion in same account. P1 from customer, can SRE triage?

ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-204 and paged @sre-oncall :rotating_light:

eugene: grabbing initial repro — asked for dig + curl from pod and bastion.

andre: from a broken app pod (kubectl exec -> dig):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> api.svc.internal.redwood +short +search
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
```

andre: from bastion in same VPC (ssh bastion):
```
$ dig +short api.svc.internal.redwood
10.2.3.4
```

josh: few likely vectors: private hosted zone misassociation / duplicate hosted zone, Route53 Resolver rules (forwarding), VPC DNS settings (dhcp options), node-local DNS/coredns caching, firewall blocking UDP/TCP 53 or iptables on nodes. Also check if pods are using search domains that cause short name lookups to append unexpected suffixes.

eugene: ran aws checks — listing resolver rule associations for the VPC:
```
$ aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0abc123def
{
  "ResolverRuleAssociations": [
    {
      "Id": "rra-0123456789",
      "Name": "forward-to-onprem",
      "ResolverRuleId": "r-0123456789",
      "VPCId": "vpc-0abc123def",
      "Status": "ASSOCIATED"
    }
  ]
}
```

eugene: that resolver rule is in the shared-services account and forwards *.internal -> 10.10.0.5 (on-prem DNS forwarder). On-prem doesn't know about the new service we created last week, so it returns NXDOMAIN for api.svc.internal.redwood. Bastion uses AWS-provided VPC resolver (no rule applied) so it sees the correct private hosted zone. Pods/EC2 instances are honoring the resolver rule and get NXDOMAIN.

talya: aha — that matches customer report (works from bastion, fails from pods). What did we change last week?

josh: we onboarded a resolver rule in shared-services to forward customer-internal zones to on-prem for legacy services. It was associated with the PROD VPC by mistake during a rollout.

andre: mitigation plan I executed: disassociated the resolver rule from vpc-0abc123def, flushed caches on nodes, and restarted kube-dns pods. Commands:
```
$ aws route53resolver disassociate-resolver-rule --association-id rra-0123456789
# on nodes
systemd-resolve --flush-caches || true
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
# quick DNS check from a pod after restart
dig +short api.svc.internal.redwood
```

sre-oncall: confirmed after disassociation and coredns restart the pod dig returns 10.2.3.4 and healthchecks from customer now green. Customer on the call confirmed fixes.

talya: customer update posted — they validated the job success and downgraded to P2, asked for RCA.

eugene: root cause: resolver rule for *.internal in shared-services was incorrectly associated with the prod VPC — it forwarded queries to on-prem which didn't have the new record, causing NXDOMAIN.

josh: next steps / action items:
- Add association guardrails: terraform change to prevent shared-services resolver-rule from being associated with prod VPCs without explicit approval. (owner: josh)
- Add monitoring alert: route53resolver association changes for prod VPCs (owner: andre)
- Update runbook: triage checklist for NXDOMAIN from pods vs bastion (owner: talya)
- Reach out to infra/security about documenting intended forwarders and zones (owner: eugene)

talya: I'll draft the customer RCA and link these action items. Thanks all for quick response :heart:

ops-bot: INC-2026-204 status -> mitigated, severity lowered.
